caution: A failure to reproduce is not a finding that the paper is wrong. It may be a failure of the attempt.

attempts.label: DANDI:000230

inputs.what: Definitions of the gridness score, mean vector length (head-direction score), border score, the head-direction stability criterion and the shuffle used to classify cells, from the Materials and methods of Rowland et al. (2018), which the STAR Methods cite for all analysis of the electrophysiology. Methods only, no data.

Analysis details Rowland et al. (2018) leave out of their text (position and speed smoothing, 5 cm/s speed cutoff, rate map smoothing of 2 bins, head-direction tuning in 180 bins smoothed with 2 bins), from the analysis code that paper links, files analysis_helpers/tracking.py, analysis_helpers/spatial_maps.py and analysis_helpers/parameters/params_ragnihiij. Parameters only, no data.

attempts.entry_title: Optogenetic tagging of rabies-labelled MEC input cells (Jacobsen et al. 2022)
attempts.summary: The paper's optogenetic tagging results held up in this data, but its single-cell tracing and imaging results could not be tested. Entorhinal input cells to the hippocampus responded to light within 2 to 4 ms, including a grid cell, and grid, head direction and border cells were present. The border cell and the example cells' values rest on assumptions about the shuffle and about which unlabelled laser epoch the figure uses. How reliably single starter cells are labelled, which inputs they receive and the two-photon imaging could not be tested, because the dandiset holds only the electrophysiology of two mice. Of the minor claims, a cell followed across sessions and the non-responsive cells matched in part.
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Jacobsen, Nair, Obenhaus, Donato, Slettmoen, Moser and Moser (2022) that can be tested on dandiset 000230, which holds nine optrode sessions of two mice with the 12 curated MEC units shown in Figures 5C, S3 and S4. It classifies the units as grid, head direction and border cells, and measures their open-field rates and their latency and fidelity to laser pulses. The histology of the single-cell tracing and the two-photon imaging are not in the dandiset.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Jacobsen et al. (2022) from dandiset 000230

outcomes.statement: In mice with widespread RABV-ChR2-YFP expression, MEC recordings include grid, head direction and border cells, so the network as a whole is not disrupted by the rabies expression.
outcomes.source: Results, The functional properties of input cells to birthdate-defined cell populations can be determined with optogenetics in vivo, paragraph 3; Figures 5C and S4
outcomes.quote: We found several functional cell types, including grid, head direction, and border cells (Figures 5C and S4), indicating that the network as a whole was not affected by the widespread rabies expression
outcomes.notes: Under the standard shuffle the 12 units include 2 grid cells (T1 C89 and T1 C50 of 58313, day 19, gridness 0.854 and 0.996), 2 head direction cells (T4 C16, day 17, mean vector length 0.912 and half-session stability 0.97; and the 70375 unit of day 15 session 2, 0.123 and 0.675) and 1 border cell (T4 C50, day 18, border score 0.656 against a shuffle threshold of 0.555). Under the literal shuffle T4 C50 falls short (0.656 against 0.663), giving 2 grid, 1 head direction and 0 border cells, so the outcome rests on the shuffle reading. Under the standard shuffle each unit the figures name is classed as the paper names it. For T4 C16 the literal shuffle's 95th percentile of the mean vector length is 0.762 and its largest value 0.912, the observed score, against 0.225 and 0.272 under the standard shuffle. The standard shuffle is lenient for a weakly tuned cell, as the day 15 session 2 unit of 70375 passes at 0.123 against 0.082. Taking the open field as its first 1800 s changes no class. The part of the statement about the network as a whole cannot be tested, as the dandiset holds only the 12 curated units shown in the figures, so finding one unit of each type partly reflects what was deposited.
deviations: Rowland et al. (2018), Materials and methods, classification into functional classes, shift spikes "by a random interval between ± 20 s, with the end of the session wrapped to the beginning"; the archdata code has no spatial shuffle. Read literally (uniform within 20 s) and as the standard shuffle of the papers Rowland et al. cite for the scores (Langston et al. 2010; Solstad et al. 2008, a shift of at least 20 s). The readings differ for the border cell; the standard shuffle is adopted as an assumption, since a shift of under 20 s leaves the spike train nearly in place and gives a null distribution close to the observed map.
Rate map bin of 2.5 cm from Rowland et al. (2018), Methods, gridness score ("steps of 1 bin (2.5 cm)"); the linked code's parameter file gives 2 cm. The text was followed.
Smoothing, speed cutoff and tuning bins from the archdata code (see inputs), as neither paper's text gives them.

The open field is taken as the whole position series, an assumption, as the files have no open-field epoch and the Methods give its length only as "approximately 30 min". The other reading, the first 1800 s, was run for all 12 units and changes no class.

outcomes.statement: Among the cells that responded to laser stimulation with a 2 to 4 ms latency, a sign of direct ChR2 activation and so of a monosynaptic projection to the hippocampus, were grid cells.
outcomes.source: Results, The functional properties of input cells to birthdate-defined cell populations can be determined with optogenetics in vivo, paragraph 3; Figure 5C
outcomes.quote: Cells that responded robustly to laser stimulation with a 2- to 4-ms latency (demonstrating direct activation as opposed to later, ... included grid cells (Figure 5C)
outcomes.notes: Under reading (a), TTL onset, 9 unit-sessions are responsive (latency 1.8 to 4.4 ms, fidelity at least 11.64%), among them the grid cell T1 C89 (day 19) at 2.75 ms and 40.73%, with no spike in the 10 ms before any pulse. Under reading (b), TTL offset, latencies are about 1.06 ms shorter and T1 C89 (1.70 ms) is not responsive; 3 unit-sessions are, none a grid cell. T1 C89 is a grid cell under both shuffle readings.
deviations: The first TTL event of each laser epoch starts at the epoch start and lasts 45 ms to 1.9 s; it is not a pulse onset and is left out, leaving 275 pulses in a 120 s epoch.

outcomes.statement: Three example responsive cells of mouse 58313 had these open-field rates, latencies and fidelities; a grid cell (T1 C89, 19 days) 1.10 Hz, 2.75 ms, 40.73%; a high-rate cell (T1 C57, 17 days) 12.67 Hz, 3.90 ms, 35.64%; a low-rate cell (T1 C52, 17 days) 0.30 Hz, 2.65 ms, 11.64%.
outcomes.source: Figure 5C
outcomes.inferred: Values printed in the panels of Figure 5C, read from the PDF; the legend names the cells and days but no sentence gives the values.
outcomes.notes: The files keep the tetrode and cluster labels, and each day of 58313 has one session, so the units are found by label. Under reading (a) all nine values are within tolerance with T1 C57 from the second laser epoch of day 17 and T1 C52 from the first. Pooling both epochs, T1 C57 still matches (4.237 ms, 32.545%) but T1 C52's latency (2.358 ms) falls 0.03 ms below its tolerance. In epoch 1 T1 C57 gives 4.651 ms and 29.455%, and in epoch 2 T1 C52 gives 2.109 ms and 13.455%, so no single epoch fits both. The file does not tell the epochs apart, as both carry "N/A" for the power and have the same pulses (median width 1.0625 ms, as in the other files). The units fire at different rates in the two epochs (T1 C57 12.72 against 9.93 Hz, T4 C16 2.32 against 0.37 Hz), which does not establish the laser power of either. The criterion allows trying each of a day's sessions; taking a laser epoch per cell within one session goes beyond it, and the outcome rests on that choice. Under reading (b) no unit has all three values within tolerance.
deviations: The day-17 file holds two laser epochs with no power label, and the paper does not say which Figure 5C uses. Each epoch and both together were run; the outcome takes the epoch per cell, an assumption. This is asked of the paper's authors (findings).

outcomes.statement: The firing properties of one input cell stayed stable across six sessions on three days (14, 15 and 16 days after the rabies injection); it responded to every laser session with a latency of 2.50 to 2.95 ms.
outcomes.source: Results, The functional properties of input cells to birthdate-defined cell populations can be determined with optogenetics in vivo, paragraph 3; Figure S3B
outcomes.quote: The firing properties of an individual input cell were also found to remain stable for at least 3 days of continuous rabies expression (Figure S3)
outcomes.notes: Each 70375 file holds one unit on tetrode 3 with a different cluster id per session (C43, C20, C17, C24, C9, C31); their mean waveforms correlate 0.918 to 0.998, but correlations with the units of 58313 reach 0.965, so the waveform does not identify the cell. With the open field as the whole position series, under reading (a) the unit is responsive in all six sessions, latencies 2.50 to 3.05 ms, and 17 of 18 values are within tolerance; the open-field rate of day 14 session 2 is 0.899 Hz against 1.06 ± 0.106. That file holds 2722 s of open field and 413 pulses. Under the other reading of the open field, its first 1800 s, run for every session, with the first 275 pulses of each session, all 18 values are within tolerance (day 14 session 2 at 1.064 Hz, 2.951 ms and 48.00%; the last 1800 s give 0.780 Hz). The first 275 pulses are not a rule the paper applied to every session, as day 15 session 1 has 278 pulses and its printed fidelity (68.71%) is what all 278 give, where the first 275 give 69.09%; the selection that matches day 14 session 2 is specific to that session. The outcome follows the whole series, the stated assumption, as the paper does not say part of a session was left out. Under reading (b) latencies are 1.44 to 1.99 ms and 11 of 18 values are within tolerance.
deviations: No cluster label is shared across sessions. The unit is taken as the same cell because each file holds this single curated unit on tetrode 3 and the Methods say the tetrodes were not turned down between these sessions ("except when trying to record from the same cell across multiple sessions, Figure S3"); the stored waveform (one channel) is consistent with this but does not separate it from the units of the other mouse.

The open field is taken as the whole position series, an assumption (see fig5c-functional-cell-types). The first 1800 s, the reading of the Methods' "approximately 30 min", was run for every session and changes the outcome to a match on all 18 values; it is not adopted, because the cut is stated nowhere and was identified from the expected values.

outcomes.statement: Some MEC cells recorded in the same area did not respond to laser stimulation, among them a head direction cell (T4 C16, 17 days, head direction score 0.81, mean vector length 0.90, peak rate 9.02 Hz, open-field rate 1.05 Hz), a border cell (T4 C50, 18 days, 1.69 Hz) and a grid cell (T1 C50, 19 days, 0.78 Hz).
outcomes.source: Figure S4
outcomes.inferred: Read from Figure S4 and its legend in the PDF (the supplement's legends are not in the text); no sentence of the main text states it.
outcomes.notes: None of T4 C16, T4 C50 and T1 C50 is responsive under either reading or any epoch (fidelity 0.00 to 1.82%), and their open-field rates match. For T4 C16 the mean vector length of the smoothed tuning map, which Rowland et al. (2018) call the head-direction score, is 0.912 with the archdata parameters, within tolerance of the mean vector length of 0.90 and outside that of the head direction score of 0.81; it is given as measured for both. The peak rate there is 10.62 Hz against 9.02 ± 0.90 Hz. Over 48 tuning settings (bins of 2 to 10 degrees, smoothing sigma 0 to 20 degrees, with and without the speed filter) the mean vector length runs from 0.857 to 0.931; the peak is in tolerance in 15 settings, all with sigma 4 to 14 degrees, and no setting puts both the peak and the mean vector length within tolerance of 9.02 Hz and 0.81. The vector length of the head directions at spikes (0.880 over all spikes, 0.923 above 5 cm/s) is within tolerance of both 0.81 and 0.90, so it does not identify the score. Two of six values miss under the cited method.
deviations: Rowland et al. (2018) define one quantity, "Mean vector length (head-direction score)"; the paper reported a head direction score and a mean vector length with different values. Both are taken as the mean vector length of the tuning map, as Rowland et al. define it, with the archdata tuning curve (2 degree bins, sigma 2 bins, no speed filter), an assumption; other bin widths, smoothing and speed filtering are shown. Asked of the paper's authors (findings).

outcomes.statement: Laser-responsive cells with clear spatial firing patterns could be identified for at least 19 days after the rabies injection.
outcomes.source: Results, The functional properties of input cells to birthdate-defined cell populations can be determined with optogenetics in vivo, paragraph 3; Figure 5C
outcomes.quote: responsive cells with clear spatial firing patterns could be identified for at least 19 days after the rabies injection (Figure 5C)
outcomes.notes: The one session at 19 days or more (58313, day 19) holds T1 C89, responsive under reading (a) (2.75 ms, 40.73%, within 2 to 4 ms) and a grid cell under both shuffle readings. Under reading (b) its latency is 1.70 ms and no unit of that session qualifies.

outcomes.statement: In the optogenetic experiments, input cells could be detected in the MEC from about 2 weeks after the rabies injection.
outcomes.source: Results, The functional properties of input cells to birthdate-defined cell populations can be determined with optogenetics in vivo, paragraph 3
outcomes.quote: In these experiments, input cells could be detected in the MEC from approximately 2 weeks after the rabies injection.
outcomes.notes: Under reading (a) the earliest session with a responsive unit is on day 14 (70375, both sessions, 2.83 ms and 27.64%, 3.05 ms and 46.49%), within 12.6 to 15.4 days. Under reading (b), with the 2 to 4 ms window, it is day 17. The dandiset holds no session before day 14 and only the curated units the figures show, so the test cannot fail on the early side and cannot show that responsive cells were absent earlier; the result is consistent with the statement.

outcomes.statement: With the single-cell protocol, starter cells could be identified conclusively in 15 of 31 animals (48%), and each of these had four or fewer starter cells.
outcomes.source: Results, A virus-based method for targeting a single cell and identifying its inputs, paragraph 4; Figure 2A
outcomes.quote: With this approach, we could unambiguously target four or fewer starter cells in 48% of animals (15 of 31) (Figure 2A)
outcomes.notes: Needs the histology of the 31 single-cell animals. The dandiset holds only nine optrode sessions of two mice; the paper's Data and code availability section deposits only the electrophysiology and names no other archive. The counts printed in Table S1 are the paper, not data.

outcomes.statement: Among the 31 single-cell animals, 4 had zero starter cells, 5 one, 2 two, 2 three and 2 four, and 16 were inconclusive.
outcomes.source: Figure 2A; Table S1
outcomes.inferred: Counts read from the bar chart of Figure 2A and the Starter cells column of Table S1; no sentence gives them.
outcomes.notes: Histology not in the dandiset nor deposited elsewhere (see fig2a-four-or-fewer-starters).

outcomes.statement: A single starter cell was labelled in 5 of the 15 conclusive animals (33%), an overall success rate of 16% (5 of 31) for targeting a single hippocampal cell.
outcomes.source: Results, A virus-based method for targeting a single cell and identifying its inputs, paragraph 4; Figure 2A
outcomes.quote: In this group, a single starter cell was labeled 33% of the time (5 of 15) (Figure 2A), resulting in an overall success rate of 16% (5 of 31) for targeting a single cell in the hippocampus
outcomes.notes: Histology not in the dandiset nor deposited elsewhere (see fig2a-four-or-fewer-starters).

outcomes.statement: No starter cells were found in the MEC.
outcomes.source: Results, A virus-based method for targeting a single cell and identifying its inputs, paragraph 3
outcomes.quote: No starter cells were found in the MEC.
outcomes.notes: Histology not in the dandiset nor deposited elsewhere (see fig2a-four-or-fewer-starters).

outcomes.statement: The number of rabies-positive cells in the ipsilateral dorsal hippocampus increases with the days after the rabies injection (Spearman R = 0.58, p = 0.0014, n = 27 animals).
outcomes.source: Figure 2B, left, and legend; Results, A virus-based method for targeting a single cell and identifying its inputs, paragraph 4
outcomes.quote: the total number of rabies-positive cells observed in the ipsilateral dorsal hippocampus increases as a function of days after the rabies injection (R = 0.58, p = 0.0014, Spearman's rho, n = 27 animals not including control animals)

statistics.n: 27 animals, single-cell animals without the four with zero starter cells, no controls

outcomes.notes: Histology counts not in the dandiset nor deposited elsewhere (see fig2a-four-or-fewer-starters).

outcomes.statement: Conclusive animals (days 26 to 30) have more rabies-positive cells in the dorsal hippocampus than the no-Cre control animals, which were all inconclusive.
outcomes.source: Figure 2B, right, and legend
outcomes.quote: the number of rabies-positive cells is larger in conclusive animals compared with control animals, which were all inconclusive (p = 0.0159, Wilcoxon rank-sum test, n = 5 conclusive and 4 control animals
outcomes.notes: Histology counts not in the dandiset nor deposited elsewhere (see fig2a-four-or-fewer-starters).

outcomes.statement: The spread of rabies-positive cells along the longitudinal axis of the dorsal hippocampus increases with days after the rabies injection (Spearman r = 0.54, p = 0.0036, n = 27 animals).
outcomes.source: Figure S2A, left, and legend; Results, A virus-based method for targeting a single cell and identifying its inputs, paragraph 4
outcomes.quote: longer expression times of the RABV increased the number of rabies-positive cells (Figure 2B), the anatomical area over which they were found in the dorsal hippocampus (Figure S2A)
outcomes.notes: Histology not in the dandiset nor deposited elsewhere (see fig2a-four-or-fewer-starters).

outcomes.statement: The spread of rabies-positive cells in the hippocampus is larger in conclusive animals (days 26 to 30) than in no-Cre controls (p = 0.0317, Wilcoxon rank sum, 5 and 4 animals).
outcomes.source: Figure S2A, right, and legend; Results, A virus-based method for targeting a single cell and identifying its inputs, paragraph 5
outcomes.quote: Although some spurious rabies expression was observed in the hippocampus, the number and anatomical ... spread of rabies-positive cells was significantly lower than in conclusive animals (Figures 2B and S2A)
outcomes.notes: Histology not in the dandiset nor deposited elsewhere (see fig2a-four-or-fewer-starters).

outcomes.statement: Longer rabies expression increases the number of input cells labelled in the MEC; MEC-labelled cells appear only in animals with 22 or more days of rabies.
outcomes.source: Results, A virus-based method for targeting a single cell and identifying its inputs, paragraph 4; Figure S2B
outcomes.quote: As expected, longer expression times of the RABV increased ... as well as the number of input cells labeled in the more distant MEC (Figure S2B)
outcomes.notes: Histology not in the dandiset nor deposited elsewhere (see fig2a-four-or-fewer-starters).

outcomes.statement: In no-Cre control animals rabies did not spread to the MEC, even with 2.5 times the volume and a higher titre (10^11 infectious particles/ml) of helper virus.
outcomes.source: Results, A virus-based method for targeting a single cell and identifying its inputs, paragraph 5; Figures S2B and S1C
outcomes.quote: and spread to the MEC did not occur (Figure S2B), not even when a larger volume (2.5 times more) and higher titer (1011 infectious particles/ml) of the helper virus were used (Figure S1C)
outcomes.notes: Histology of the control animals not in the dandiset nor deposited elsewhere.

outcomes.statement: Without Cre and helper virus, RABV-tdTomato alone produces no tdTomato expression in the hippocampus, so unpseudotyped rabies virus does not contribute to the labelling.
outcomes.source: Results, A virus-based method for targeting a single cell and identifying its inputs, paragraph 5; Figure S1A, left
outcomes.quote: This can be due to the presence of unpseudotyped RABVs ... The former does not seem to be an issue here (Figure S1A)
outcomes.notes: Histology of mouse 72359 not in the dandiset nor deposited elsewhere.

outcomes.statement: Diluted AAV-CKII-Cre injected in utero at E13 leaves only a few Cre-expressing cells in the adult hippocampus.
outcomes.source: Results, A virus-based method for targeting a single cell and identifying its inputs, paragraph 2; Figure S1B
outcomes.quote: only a few cells express Cre in the adult hippocampus of these animals (Figure S1B)
outcomes.notes: Histology of mice 58482 and 58483 not in the dandiset nor deposited elsewhere.

outcomes.statement: The inputs of a single starter cell reflect its identity; a CA3 pyramidal starter cell (16 days) and a CA2 stratum oriens interneuron starter cell (30 days) in neighbouring regions received very different sets of hippocampal inputs.
outcomes.source: Results, A virus-based method for targeting a single cell and identifying its inputs, paragraph 4; Figure 3B and D
outcomes.quote: The identity of the inputs reflected the identity of the starter cell (Figures 3 and 4), which is an important indication that the RABV is indeed transsynaptic. For example, the constellation of inputs a single pyramidal neuron and a single interneuron received was very different despite them being located in neighboring regions (distal CA3 and CA2) in the hippocampus (Figure 3)
outcomes.notes: Histology of animals 59457 and 60219 not in the dandiset nor deposited elsewhere.

outcomes.statement: After 20 days of rabies, a single granule cell starter received input from one other granule cell more than 320 um away along the longitudinal axis.
outcomes.source: Results, Targeting single starter cells in the hippocampus highlights granule-granule cell connectivity, paragraph 1; Figure 4A legend
outcomes.quote: After 20 days of rabies expression, one granule cell was found to receive input from another granule cell located several hundred micrometers away along the longitudinal axis of the hippocampus (Figure 4A)
outcomes.notes: Histology of animal 60047 not in the dandiset nor deposited elsewhere.

outcomes.statement: After 26 days, a single granule cell starter had 35 hippocampal input cells, 80% of them granule cells; subtracting the highest background count of the controls (18) still leaves 58.8% granule cell inputs.
outcomes.source: Results, Targeting single starter cells in the hippocampus highlights granule-granule cell connectivity, paragraph 1; Figure 4B
outcomes.quote: After 26 days (in a different animal), the virus had spread to a total of 35 input cells in the hippocampus, 80% of which were other granule cells (Figure 4B). Even when accounting for background expression, granule cells were still the dominant input type
outcomes.notes: Histology of animal 60652 not in the dandiset nor deposited elsewhere.

outcomes.statement: Many granule cell inputs lay in the subgranular zone, suggesting immature granule cells; 1 of 1 after 20 days and 11 of 28 after 26 days.
outcomes.source: Results, Targeting single starter cells in the hippocampus highlights granule-granule cell connectivity, paragraph 1
outcomes.quote: a substantial number of their inputs was found in the subgranular zone (1 of 1 granule cell inputs after 20 days, 11 of 28 after 26 days)
outcomes.notes: Histology of animals 60047 and 60652 not in the dandiset nor deposited elsewhere.

outcomes.statement: A single dentate gyrus starter cell (possibly a molecular layer perforant path-associated interneuron) had 34 hippocampal input cells and 4 input cells in the MEC after 28 days.
outcomes.source: Figure 4C legend
outcomes.quote: The pie chart (center left) shows the proportions of hippocampal input cell types to the single starter cell highlighted on the left 28 days after the rabies injection (n = 34 input cells in the hippocampus to a single starter cell)
outcomes.notes: Histology of animal 60259 not in the dandiset nor deposited elsewhere.

outcomes.statement: When targeting single cells, cell damage was typically not seen until more than 30 days after the rabies injection; dendritic blebbing appeared at 34 days.
outcomes.source: Discussion, paragraph 4; Figure 7A legend
outcomes.quote: we typically did not see cell damage until more than 30 days after the rabies injection when attempting to target single cells (Figure 7A)
outcomes.notes: Histology of mouse 60388 and the single-cell animals not in the dandiset nor deposited elsewhere.

outcomes.statement: With more Cre virus in utero and more helper virus in the adult, populations of birthdate-matched hippocampal cells (E12, E14) could be targeted, as could a general population when Cre was given with the helper virus in the adult; both approaches led to broad labelling of input cells in the superficial MEC.
outcomes.source: Results, The functional properties of input cells to birthdate-defined cell populations can be determined with optogenetics in vivo, paragraph 2; Figures 5B, 6A, S1A and S3A
outcomes.quote: Both approaches led to broad labeling of these populations’ input cells in the superficial MEC (Figures 5B, 6A, S1A, and S3A)
outcomes.notes: Needs the histology of mice 58313, 58253, 58695 and 70375. The dandiset holds recordings of 58313 and 70375 but no histology; nothing is deposited elsewhere.

outcomes.statement: Two-photon imaging through a prism in a head-fixed mouse identified several MEC cells expressing RABV-GCaMP6f, that is, cells projecting to an E14 birthdate-matched hippocampal population; five such cells were imaged 19 days after the rabies injection, with different activity onsets.
outcomes.source: Results, In vivo two-photon calcium imaging enables functional detection of distant input cells to birthdate-defined cell populations, paragraph 1; Figure 6B
outcomes.quote: This enabled us to perform ... imaging in awake, head-fixed mice and identify several cells projecting to a population of birthdate-matched cells in the hippocampus (Figure 6B)
outcomes.notes: The two-photon imaging of mouse 58253 is not in the dandiset, and the paper names no deposit for it.

outcomes.statement: With GCaMP6m expressed in the MEC by AAV and RABV-tdTomato injected into the hippocampus, a two-photon miniscope identified in vivo an MEC cell expressing both, an input to the targeted hippocampal starter cells, next to a GCaMP6m-only cell, 29 days after the rabies injection.
outcomes.source: Results, In vivo two-photon calcium imaging enables functional detection of distant input cells to birthdate-defined cell populations, paragraph 2; Figure 7B
outcomes.quote: When the RABV reached the MEC, we were able to identify a cell expressing both the calcium indicator and tdTomato in vivo with a two-photon miniscope (Figure 7B
outcomes.notes: The miniscope imaging of mouse 60388 is not in the dandiset, and the paper names no deposit for it.

findings.statement: The dandiset holds only the optrode recordings of two mice (58313, 70375), and of these only the 12 curated units shown in Figures 5C, S3 and S4 (the files say "Only a curated subset of tasks and/or units are exported"). The histology of the single-cell tracing (Figures 2 to 4, S1, S2, Tables S1, S2) and the two-photon imaging (Figures 6 and 7) are not in it, and the paper names no other deposit, so 21 of the paper's 28 claims cannot be tested.
The open field part of each session is not an epoch; the epochs table holds only the PhotoStim epochs. Its span can only be inferred from the position series.

The two laser epochs of the day-17 session of mouse 58313 carry "N/A" for the power label that the dandiset description says sessions carry; the other eight files carry "10Hz20mW". Which epoch Figure 5C uses cannot be told from the files, as both epochs have the same pulse widths and intervals.
The first laser TTL event of every PhotoStim epoch has its onset at exactly the epoch start time and lasts 45 ms to 1.9 s (ten such events in nine files), where every other event lasts 1.0 to 1.1 ms.
The STAR Methods describe 1 ms light pulses "at 10 Hz continuously"; the TTL events show trains of 6 pulses at 10 Hz every 2.6 s (275 pulses in a 120 s epoch).
The LFP timestamps run backwards 2 to 4 times within each file and end at 120 to 180 s, although each LFP series has 510,250 to 815,750 samples 4 ms apart (over 2000 s).
Units waveform_mean is labelled volts but its values have a peak-to-trough of 31 to 41 for the 70375 unit and 34 to 243 for the units of 58313, which cannot be volts; the scale is not stated.

For day 14 session 2 of mouse 70375 the file holds 2722 s of open field and 413 pulses. The paper's printed rate, latency and fidelity for that session (1.06 Hz, 2.95 ms, 48.00%) are what the first 1800 s and the first 275 pulses give (1.064 Hz, 2.95 ms, 48.00%); over the whole file the values are 0.899 Hz, 3.05 ms and 46.49%. The paper does not say part of the session was left out. The first 275 pulses are not a rule applied to every session, as for day 15 session 1 (278 pulses) the printed fidelity of 68.71% is what all 278 pulses give.

Version 0.220426.0814 of the dandiset holds 18 assets, the nine sessions under the subject ids 58313 and 70375 and again under the hashed ids of version 0.220422.0713. The pinned version 0.220506.1516 holds each session once.

The positions of the day-17 session of mouse 58313 span 76 x 75 cm, where the other eight sessions span about 94 x 95 cm, consistent with the 1 x 1 m open field of the Methods. The files do not say whether a different box was used.

B8 (border score walls are the edges of the tracked extent; a uniformly firing cell scores 0.48), stated in the helper docstring; the shuffle thresholds take in that baseline, so no change to the method. B9 (latency_fidelity uses side="right", immaterial at a 48 kHz spike clock), no change. Cell numbers in the reasons below refer to the round-1 notebook; in the current notebook cells 11, 14, 16, 19, 21, 23 and 25 are cells 13, 18, 21, 26, 29, 32 and 35.

The full executed notebook of the revised run (39 cells), with its conclusions and summary, the helper module, the README, the attempt record and the claims file, with the paper. Report in transcripts/jacobsen-2022/verifier-2-report.md. The verifier found no place where the claims file misreads the paper, so no question was added. Points without a claim of their own, with the response. Cell 6 said the LFP timestamps run backwards 3 or 4 times within each file, where cell 5 prints 2 for both day-15 files; corrected to 2 to 4. The Summary said waveform_mean holds peak-to-trough 31 to 41, printed only for the 70375 unit; cell 25 now prints it for the units of 58313 too (34 to 243) and the Summary and finding give both. The README said the notebook takes about four minutes where it printed 106 s; this run printed 181 s, of which the two shuffle runs take 83 s each, and the README now says about three minutes. The round-1 reasons cite the round-1 cell numbers; the round-1 entry now maps them to the current cells, and the reasons are left in the verifier's words. The verifier still cannot view the rendered rate maps; the grid and border calls rest on the printed scores, so no change.

paper_notes.statement: Question for the paper's authors. Figure S4 gives T4 C16 a head direction score of 0.81 and a mean vector length of 0.90, but Rowland et al. (2018), which the STAR Methods cite for both, define one quantity, "Mean vector length (head-direction score)". How is the head direction score computed, and what binning and smoothing give the tuning curve's peak rate of 9.02 Hz? Here the tuning-map mean vector length is 0.912 and the peak rate 10.62 Hz with the archdata parameters; the peak reaches 9.02 ± 0.90 Hz only with smoothing sigmas of 4 to 14 degrees, where the mean vector length is 0.897 to 0.912.

Question for the paper's authors. The day-17 session of mouse 58313 has two laser epochs. Which epoch, at which power, gives the latency and fidelity of T1 C57 and T1 C52 in Figure 5C? Here T1 C57 matches the second epoch (3.90 ms, 35.64%) and T1 C52 the first (2.65 ms, 11.64%).

Question for the paper's authors. Rowland et al. (2018), cited for the cell classification, shift spike trains "by a random interval between ± 20 s". Was the shift within 20 s, or at least 20 s as in the papers they cite? The border cell T4 C50 passes the second (0.656 against 0.555) and not the first (0.656 against 0.663).

entries.name: jacobsen-2022
entries.title: Optogenetic tagging of rabies-labelled MEC input cells (Jacobsen et al. 2022)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Jacobsen, Nair, Obenhaus, Donato, Slettmoen, Moser and Moser (2022) that can be tested on dandiset 000230, which holds nine optrode sessions of two mice with the 12 curated MEC units shown in Figures 5C, S3 and S4. It classifies the units as grid, head direction and border cells, and measures their open-field rates and their latency and fidelity to laser pulses. The histology of the single-cell tracing and the two-photon imaging are not in the dandiset.
